name: Wyoming Voice
description: Wyoming Voice runs the two speech services a local Home Assistant Assist pipeline needs: wyoming-faster-whisper for speech-to-text on port 10300 and wyoming-piper for text-to-speech on port 10200, each spoken to over the Wyoming protocol. Nothing is sent to a cloud service, so Assist and Voice PE hardware keep working without internet access.

notes.text: There is no web interface. Add the container twice in Home Assistant under Settings > Devices & Services > Add Integration > Wyoming Protocol: once as <container-ip> port 10300 (speech-to-text) and once as <container-ip> port 10200 (text-to-speech), then select both in Settings > Voice assistants.

The Whisper model (small-int8) and the Piper voice (en_US-lessac-medium) are downloaded during install into /opt/wyoming-voice, so the first Assist request is not a cold start. To use a different model or voice, edit --model in /etc/systemd/system/wyoming-faster-whisper.service or --voice in /etc/systemd/system/wyoming-piper.service and restart that service; it is fetched on next start.

Transcription is CPU-only and scales with core count. small-int8 on 4 cores transcribes roughly 1.8x faster than realtime; drop to base-int8 or tiny-int8 on fewer cores, and raise them if responses feel slow.
Both services listen on 0.0.0.0 with no authentication, because the Wyoming protocol has none. Keep the container on a trusted network segment.
